messages:
nina: Quick follow-up from the rate-limiter RFC: we saw a revoke -> immediate multi-shard re-admit pattern causing eviction churn.
cal: So revokes aren't visible to other schedulers fast enough?
nina: Right. Revoke writes to central KV but schedulers read lazily; abusive clients bounce to other shards and get new leases.
don: I sketched three mitigation ideas: 1) short-lived KV tombstone + local cache, 2) lightweight push fanout on revoke to prime caches, 3) probation fallback instead of hard deny while cache warms.
cal: Fanout is nice but best-effort. Tombstone + cache seems robust; cache avoids KV on the happy path.
nina: Admission flow proposal:
```
1) fast local token check
2) consult local revocation cache (LRU)
3) if miss, async read tombstone KV and route to probation path (reduced throughput) while we fetch
4) if tombstone present -> deny or hard-quarantine (configurable)
```
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Planned canary: revocation-cache + probation fallback to 15% of edge nodes at 04:00 UTC for 90m.
don: TTL debate: 15s/30s/60s. Suggest default 30s and per-tenant override for high-severity cases.
cal: Need appeal/rollback: manual ops retract + automated appeals go into probation and require verification to lift.
nina: Metrics to add: tombstone read QPS, cache hit ratio, new-lease-after-revoke rate, probation admission rate. Action items: cal -> micro-RFC with TTLs; don -> prototype cache + async fetch; nina -> ops playbook for retract/appeal. Keep canary probation-only to avoid mass denies.
